text:
Kirill Kaprizov has a point in 12 straight games, 23 in all, and the Wild have points in 12 in a row with him driving it. He has 40 points in 23 games, 13 of them on the power play, and Minnesota takes 57% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) at five on five when he's out there. That part is real. His chances are up too, 1.70 expected goals per 60 against 1.32 last season.

What won't last is the finishing. He's shooting 23% against 17% a year ago, and his team has scored 10.7 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Our talent range puts his true scoring rate well below the 4.89 points per 60 he's running at, and still has him finishing around 113 points. That tells you how high the floor is.

Lately he's been the passer: 15 assists in his last 10. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 87th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season, carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries. Watch the blue line when he has it.
